title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Cal Poly Pomona spaces for studying, making, recreation, art, and outdoor meet-ups, each supported by a direct campus or Associated Students source.

cards.entity_name: George and Sakaye Aratani Japanese Garden
cards.title: Pause by the Japanese Garden
cards.subtitle: Cal Poly Pomona campus
cards.notes: Use the bridges, pond, and small amphitheater as an easy outdoor meeting point; check campus event or reservation guidance before planning a formal gathering.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped 1.3-acre garden with a pond, waterfall, bridges, and walkways.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly Pomona describes the George and Sakaye Aratani Japanese Garden as a 1.3-acre garden with a pond, waterfall, bridges, walkways, fountain, and small amphitheater.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus venue; the university lists it among special venues, so confirm any event or photography requirements in advance.

cards.title: Meet at the Rose Garden gazebo
cards.subtitle: North of the CLA building
cards.notes: Choose the gazebo and floral rows for a daylight outdoor rendezvous or a quick photo stop, then leave the garden as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A rose garden with a white gazebo and more than 230 rose varieties.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says the Rose Garden north of the CLA building has a white wood gazebo and more than 230 rose varieties tended by floriculture students.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus venue; confirm reservation requirements before organizing a group activity.

cards.title: Use Union Plaza as a waypoint
cards.subtitle: Original Kellogg stable building
cards.notes: Set a meet-up at the Russell & Ruth Mawby Fountain, then use the courtyard’s long central path to orient the next stop on campus.
cards.short_summary: A courtyard in the original Kellogg stable building, anchored by a named fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly Pomona identifies Union Plaza Courtyard as being in the original Kellogg stable building and says it contains the Russell & Ruth Mawby Fountain.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus courtyard; comply with posted event and reservation rules.

cards.title: Start a study session at the Library
cards.subtitle: Building 15
cards.notes: Use the Library’s study-room reservation link for a group plan, or begin with its computers and service desks when you need a focused campus base.
cards.short_summary: The main library offers study rooms, computers, collections, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library site provides a study-room reservation link, and its about page notes more than 40 study rooms and hundreds of computers.
cards.access_notes: Building 15; consult the Library’s current hours and reserve a room when needed.

cards.title: Book a Library group study room
cards.subtitle: University Library, Building 15
cards.notes: Gather two or more people, reserve one room through the Library system, and keep the session within the current three-hour maximum.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Library rooms for small groups working together.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library’s group-study-room policy requires a group of two or more and sets a maximum reservation length of three hours.
cards.access_notes: Reservations use a CPP email confirmation; bookings outside Library hours are not honored.

cards.title: Make a prototype in the Maker Studio
cards.subtitle: University Library, second floor
cards.notes: Schedule a tour or reserve the studio before bringing a project; its listed tools include 3D printing, laser cutting, sewing, and vinyl work.
cards.short_summary: A Library makerspace for hands-on prototyping across majors.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Innovation Idea Labs says the Maker Studio is on the University Library’s second floor and lists 3D printing, laser, soldering, sewing, vinyl, and other equipment.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday through Friday, noon to 5 p.m.; reservations or tours are available through SIIL.

cards.title: Take a break in the Games Room
cards.subtitle: Bronco Student Center, Building 35-1110
cards.notes: Plan a low-key break with billiards, consoles, or air hockey, and check ASI’s current facility-hours page before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Bronco Student Center recreation room with games and the campus Lost and Found.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI says the Games Room in the Bronco Student Center offers billiards, gaming consoles, air hockey, and serves as the official CPP Lost and Found.
cards.access_notes: Located in Building 35-1110; ASI publishes current Games Room hours separately and notes that hours may change.

cards.title: Plan an open-swim pool break
cards.subtitle: Bronco Recreation and Intramural Complex
cards.notes: Check current pool hours and lifeguard availability, then bring only permitted equipment or use the listed checkout items during open swim.
cards.short_summary: A 10-lane lap and recreation pool with an outdoor lounge area.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI describes the BRIC Pool and Poolside Lounge as having 10 lap lanes, a recreational swim area, and lounge furniture; pool use requires operating hours and a lifeguard on duty.
cards.access_notes: Use only during operating hours when a lifeguard is on duty; follow ASI pool rules and current hours.

cards.title: Try a route at Bronco Peak
cards.subtitle: Inside the Bronco Recreation and Intramural Complex
cards.notes: Check in with staff first; new climbers can use Try-A-Climb, while later open climbing requires the listed orientation and safety steps.
cards.short_summary: The BRIC’s indoor climbing wall and bouldering feature.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI identifies Bronco Peak as the BRIC climbing wall and says Try-A-Climb is a free program with no prerequisites; it also requires new users to check in with staff.
cards.access_notes: Check current open-wall hours; ASI requires an orientation and belay class before open climbing, with staff check-in for new climbers.

cards.entity_name: W. Keith & Janet Kellogg University Art Gallery
cards.title: See what is on view at Kellogg Gallery
cards.subtitle: Building 35A, 3801 West Temple Ave.
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition before visiting, then use the gallery’s contact details to confirm access or arrange a self-guided or group visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery presenting exhibitions and maintaining a collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official site identifies the W. Keith & Janet Kellogg University Art Gallery, while its contact page lists its Building 35A campus address.
cards.source_title: About the W. Keith & Janet Kellogg University Art Gallery
cards.access_notes: Gallery access and exhibition schedules can vary; confirm current details with the gallery before visiting.
